title: Pacific Atlantic Water Flow
summary: Find every cell of a height map from which rain can flow to both the Pacific and the Atlantic.

tests.explain: Rain on (2,2), height 5, can run to (1,2) (height 3) and on to (0,2) (height 2) on the top edge: the Pacific. It can also run straight to (3,2) on the bottom edge: the Atlantic. (0,0) borders only the Pacific, and all its neighbours are higher, so it is not in the answer.
A single cell touches all four edges, so it borders both oceans.
In a single row every cell touches the top edge (Pacific) and the bottom edge (Atlantic), so every cell counts.

hints: Searching from every cell separately repeats the same work up to m·n times. Turn the question around: which cells can each ocean be reached from?
Start a search from all the cells on the Pacific edges at once and move to a neighbour only if it is at least as high (water could flow from it to you). Do the same for the Atlantic edges.
A cell is in the answer if both searches reached it. Return its [row, col]; the order of the pairs doesn't matter.

complexity.time: O(m·n): two searches, each visiting every cell at most once
complexity.space: O(m·n): two visited grids and the search stack
